title: Rainforest Connection's Guardian acoustic AI sends chainsaw alerts to community patrols; logging in West Sumatra may have stopped as a result
summary: RFCx Guardian sensors detect chainsaws with AI and alert patrols; a 2021 Reuters report from Solok, West Sumatra quotes a patroller that logging stopped. No dated intervention is documented.
account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered 'Guardian' acoustic sensors that, in its own words, use 'sound & artificial intelligence' to track chainsaws, vehicle engines, hunting dogs and gunshots and to send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that 'an agent nearby' can respond. RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 (impact page) or 750,000 (guardian page) hectares across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. The only non-vendor account fetched is a Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier: audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds, and an alert goes to community patrols; patroller Jasrialdi said logging 'has totally stopped' in the area, and the head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said he would like to expand the 'early-warning system'. The same report attributes the decline in logging to a wider enforcement crackdown as well, and says RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove the system curbs logging. No park authority, ministry or court document records a specific alert leading to an interception, so no event is recorded; the date used is the publication date of the Reuters report.
purpose: Real-time acoustic detection of illegal logging and poaching sounds so that rangers or community patrols can respond; the reported benefit is the intended one.
system: Rainforest Connection Guardian bioacoustic monitoring with cloud AI sound classification and app alerts
model_version: Guardian G1 (2015-2019, repurposed smartphones), G2 (2020-2025), G3 (2026-present) per rfcx.org
deployer: Community forest patrols and the West Sumatra forestry department (Solok regency, Indonesia); RFCx partners in other countries
location: Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia (reported deployment); global program
segment: Non-profit conservation technology with community and government partners
taxonomy_note: Forest protection from illegal logging fits environmental sustainability. Evidence is the maker's own site plus a single news report (Thomson Reuters Foundation via The Straits Times); the patroller's statement that logging stopped is not attributed by the report to the AI alone, and no authority record of an intervention was found.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an attributable event; no individual outcome is documented.
General benefit; the West Sumatra patrol's reported easier work is not tied to a dated alert or action.
General benefit; RFCx's hectare figures are self-reported aggregates with no independent evaluation.

ai_role.statement: RFCx's own pages describe AI classification of streamed audio generating app alerts for responders; the 2021 Reuters report confirms the mechanism (AI picks out chainsaw sounds, patrols are alerted) at the Solok site and quotes a patroller that logging stopped, while also crediting a government enforcement crackdown. Apart from that single news item, only the maker's account was fetched; no park authority, ministry or court record of an AI-triggered interception was found, and RFCx itself said in 2021 that peer-review data to prove the effect was still being collected.
